name: Blackened Chicken with Mango Salsa

intro_html:
Here is a dinner that tastes like a vacation and costs like a Tuesday. Blackened chicken brings the heat, a fresh mango salsa cools it right back down, and a bed of cilantro lime rice makes the whole thing stick to your ribs. That contrast is what keeps you out of the drive-thru line at six o'clock.

The numbers do the talking, and they are good numbers. Each of the 14 containers lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein, so this is a real meal that keeps you full instead of a sad little cup of lettuce. Spicy chicken, sweet mango, creamy avocado, all in one bowl you built with your own two hands.

shop_smart:
Chicken breast is the anchor here at 5 1/4 pounds, so grab the biggest family pack you can find and cut it down yourself. Buying it in one big pack beats picking up a stack of shrink-wrapped single trays.

This build leans on produce that ripens on your counter, so time it right. You want 3 1/2 large mangoes and 3 1/2 large avocados that give a little when you press them, not rocks and not mush. If the store only has firm ones, buy a couple days ahead and let them come around before batch day.

Cilantro shows up in two different spots, but only the 3 1/2 fresh bunches go into the salsa. The rice already carries its own cilantro and lime, so do not double buy. Nine 8.5 ounce pouches of cilantro lime rice handle the whole base and heat right in the pouch.

A jar of blackened seasoning covers the 6 tablespoons this batch needs with plenty left for next time, and about 2 limes give you all the juice the salsa wants. Round it out with the red onion and the olive oil you already keep in the pantry.
make_it:
Make the salsa first, so the flavors have time to get friendly. Dice the mango and the avocado, chop the cilantro, and mince the red onion, then add them all to a large bowl. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper, pour in about a tablespoon of the olive oil and the fresh lime juice, and toss until everything is coated. Set it aside.

Now the chicken. Dice the 5 1/4 pounds of breast into 1 inch cubes and toss with the blackened seasoning until every piece is coated. Get a large cast iron skillet hot over medium-high heat and add the rest of your olive oil. Work in batches so you do not crowd the pan, and sear the chicken about 3 minutes per side until it is no longer pink in the center and reaches 165 degrees. Let it rest while you finish the base.

Cook the cilantro lime rice right on the package instructions. Nine pouches is a lot to move at once, so run them in rounds and hold them warm. That is your bed for every bowl.
portion_html:
This makes 14 containers, and the honest way to split it even is to weigh it, not eyeball it. Cook everything, set an empty container on the kitchen scale, and zero it out. Weigh your full pot of rice, divide by 14, and drop that same weight into each container. Do the exact same with the chicken. Eyeballing scoops is how the first few boxes get robbed and the last one shows up half empty.

Spoon the mango salsa over the top of each bowl, or pack it on the side if you like it bright and fresh come lunchtime. Either way, every container comes out to the same {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein, no favorites at this table.

steps: Make the mango salsa. Dice the mango and avocado, chop the cilantro, and mince the red onion, and add them to a large bowl. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper, add about a tablespoon of the olive oil and the fresh lime juice, and toss until well combined. Set aside.
Season the chicken. Dice the chicken breast into 1 inch cubes and toss with the blackened seasoning until every piece is evenly coated.

Sear the chicken. Heat the rest of the olive oil in a large cast iron skillet over medium-high heat. Working in batches so the pan is not crowded, cook the chicken about 3 minutes per side until it is no longer pink in the center and reaches 165 degrees. Let it rest.
Cook the cilantro lime rice. Prepare the cilantro lime rice pouches according to the package instructions, running them in rounds since it is a large batch.
Build the containers. Divide the rice and chicken evenly across 14 containers by weight, then top each with the mango salsa or pack it on the side.
